title: Cover and Ghost
premise: Orsen Delacroix, a disgraced intelligence analyst who hasn't slept a full night since the operation that killed her team, receives a calendar invite from her dead handler, Marek, scheduled for tomorrow at a border checkpoint. Following it, she uncovers a plot to stage a catastrophic 'accident' during the checkpoint shift change — a cover for a syndicate laundering stolen intelligence assets. As she assembles an unlikely crew of burned operatives, a defected insider, and a grieving widow who knows too much, Orsen realizes the attack is bait designed to flush out survivors of her old unit, including the man who betrayed them. In the climax she exposes the syndicate's ledger to the world and chooses justice outside the law, letting the syndicate's own patrons destroy it, before finally sleeping through the night with a new family around her.
about_author: Casper Vane is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade near border towns and never quite stopped watching the shift changes. Vane writes thrillers about people the system discarded, and insists every plot twist was fact-checked at 3 a.m.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Insomniac Orsen receives a calendar invite from Marek — dead eleven months — for a meeting tomorrow at Kiln Crossing checkpoint. She assumes a cruel prank until the attachment contains her old case number. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into reluctant hope.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, No Home
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Flashback woven through her morning: the incident, the inquiries, the quiet firings. She decides the invite is bait but goes anyway, packing a go-bag she never unpacked. Emotional beat: a woman with nothing left to lose choosing to lose it.

chapters.title: Kiln Crossing, 06:00
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The checkpoint is ordinary — too ordinary. She watches shift change and spots a man photographing the guard rotations, then finds a chalk mark Marek used years ago. Emotional beat: the past reaching out with cold fingers.

chapters.title: Dead Men Keep Appointments
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The chalk mark leads to a locker: Marek's burner, a half-finished report, and a note: 'The accident has a date. Find the ledger before the shift changes.' Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Waited
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Marek's widow Ilse has been followed for weeks. Orsen arrives; Ilse slams the door, then opens it, holding a second burner. Emotional beat: two strangers recognizing the same wound.

chapters.title: What Marek Found
chapters.summary: Ilse and Orsen, alternating. Marek discovered a syndicate staging 'accidents' to move stolen intelligence assets across borders — and someone inside the agencies signed off. Emotional beat: the sick clarity of conspiracy.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She maps the checkpoint schedule: the attack is timed to the 14:00 rotation, when cameras lag and two commanders overlap. Emotional beat: the clock starting to tick audibly.

chapters.title: A Thief Named Pim
chapters.summary: Pim's POV. A charming ex-smuggler who owes Marek his life notices someone buying his old routes. Orsen finds him mid-con in a dockside bar. Emotional beat: reluctant recruitment, sparks of found family.

chapters.title: The Burned List
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Marek's burner holds a partial list of 'burned assets' — operatives discarded like Orsen. Two are still alive. One is already dead this morning. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt with a body count.

chapters.title: Yusuf in the Walls
chapters.summary: Yusuf's POV. A signals technician living off-grid in a decommissioned relay station has been quietly archiving the syndicate's radio chatter for a year, waiting for someone to ask. Emotional beat: loneliness rewarded at last.

chapters.title: The Word 'Accident'
chapters.summary: Orsen and Yusuf. The chatter confirms it: a tanker, the checkpoint, the 14:00 shift change — an 'accident' that erases evidence and witnesses alike. Emotional beat: horror at how tidy evil can be.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading Over Us
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Their safehouse comms are compromised; they barely escape a sweep team. Orsen realizes the syndicate isn't hunting the attack plot — it's hunting her. Emotional beat: paranoia becoming certainty.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse identifies a name in Marek's notes: Deputy Director Corvane — Orsen's former mentor. Emotional beat: betrayal landing like a physical blow.

chapters.title: Mentor, Monster
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Flashback: Corvane taught her everything, defended her after the incident — or so she thought. Now she sees he buried the truth to protect the syndicate and himself. Emotional beat: grief for a father figure who never existed.

chapters.title: Crew of the Discarded
chapters.summary: Ensemble. Orsen, Ilse, Pim, and Yusuf meet in the relay station — four people no agency wants. Orsen lays out the plan: steal the ledger, expose the plot, stop the tanker. Emotional beat: a family forming from wreckage.

chapters.title: Rehearsal at Midnight
chapters.summary: Pim's POV. Pim walks them through the checkpoint's blind spots using routes he smuggled by. Banter, friction, trust. Emotional beat: laughter in a doomed place — the first warmth.

chapters.title: The Tanker's Paper Trail
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse poses as an insurance auditor and confirms the tanker's cargo manifest is fiction — it's carrying the syndicate's archive, to be 'destroyed' in the blast. Emotional beat: quiet fury at the paperwork of murder.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Yusuf's POV. Yusuf intercepts a message meant for the syndicate's inside man at the checkpoint. The attack has been moved up — tomorrow, not next week. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The crew scrambles: the ledger is in the checkpoint's secure annex, only accessible during the shift-change overlap. They must be inside when the attack happens. Emotional beat: fear converted to focus.

chapters.title: Orsen Sleeps for Two Hours
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Ilse forces Orsen to rest before the operation. For the first time since the incident, she dreams — of Marek, saying 'you were never the mistake.' Emotional beat: fragile healing.

chapters.title: Infiltration
chapters.summary: Pim and Orsen. Disguised as freight contractors, they breach the annex during the morning lull. Pim cracks the door; Orsen finds the server cage. Emotional beat: adrenaline with a heartbeat of calm.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The ledger is worse than imagined: years of staged accidents, bought officials, and a list of future targets — including a school bus route. Emotional beat: righteous rage.

chapters.title: Copy, Don't Steal
chapters.summary: Yusuf's POV. Yusuf remotely mirrors the ledger, but the transfer trips a tripwire. Alarms arm silently. Emotional beat: the trap they knew was there, springing.

chapters.title: Corvane Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Through the annex glass, Orsen sees Corvane inspect the checkpoint — and recognize her on a monitor. He smiles. Emotional beat: the hunter and the hunted exchanging places.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The crew is sealed in the annex as the syndicate floods the sector with hired security. Pim finds a maintenance crawl; Yusuf jams the cameras. Emotional beat: terror managed by teamwork.

chapters.title: Ilse's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse walks out alone and offers herself to Corvane as Marek's 'repentant widow,' buying the others time and planting a tracker on his car. Emotional beat: courage disguised as surrender.

chapters.title: The Overlap
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The 14:00 shift change begins. The tanker rolls into the queue. Ninety minutes until detonation. Emotional beat: time becoming a physical weight.

chapters.title: Crawl Space Confessions
chapters.summary: Pim and Orsen, in the crawlspace. Pim admits he took money from the syndicate once; Orsen admits she froze during the incident and lives believe she killed her team. Emotional beat: two liars becoming honest.

chapters.title: Cutting the Fuse
chapters.summary: Yusuf's POV. Yusuf spoofs the tanker's transponder to divert it to a dead siding, buying minutes. The syndicate's detonator operator notices. Emotional beat: a chess game at lethal speed.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Kiln
chapters.summary: Orsen and Corvane. Corvane corners her at the checkpoint, offering reinstatement and absolution if she hands over the ledger. She refuses: 'You don't get to be my father and my executioner.' Emotional beat: the past finally answered.

chapters.title: Detonation Denied
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The blast is triggered — but the tanker is empty on the siding; the explosion takes only the syndicate's own archive cache. The 'accident' happens, just not to the planned victims. Emotional beat: savage, precise victory.

chapters.title: The Ledger Goes Loud
chapters.summary: Yusuf and Ilse. The mirrored ledger is pushed to every newsroom, every oversight body, every patron's inbox. The syndicate's protectors begin eating their own. Emotional beat: justice as detonation.

chapters.title: Corvane's Exit
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Rather than arrest, Orsen leaks Corvane's location to his own masters and watches him realize his patrons have chosen the ledger over him. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, cold and complete.

chapters.title: Aftermath at the Crossing
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The checkpoint reopens under new, honest command. Officials scramble; the crew scatters to safehouses. Emotional beat: exhausted, untriumphant relief.

chapters.title: What the Dead Would Say
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse buries Marek's burner at the checkpoint fence line. Orsen stands with her. Emotional beat: mourning that finally has a shape.

chapters.title: Testimony, Off the Record
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. An oversight investigator offers Orsen reinstatement. She declines — she's seen what the system does with people like her. Emotional beat: choosing the margins on purpose.

chapters.title: The Crew That Stayed
chapters.summary: Ensemble. Pim opens a legitimate freight office; Yusuf keeps the relay station as their listening post; Ilse begins writing Marek's true story. Emotional beat: found family solidifying into daily life.

chapters.title: The Last Invite
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A new calendar invite arrives — from Marek's account, dated next week. But it's from Ilse and the crew, a joke and a promise: a standing weekly dinner. Emotional beat: laughter replacing dread.

chapters.title: First Full Night
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At the dinner's end, Orsen goes home to a small apartment with a new lock and no go-bag by the door. She sleeps through the night. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.

chapters.title: Cover and Ghost
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, coda. Months later, Orsen reads a news brief: the last syndicate patron indicted. She touches the chalk mark she keeps in her pocket, a ghost's signature, and walks into the morning shift change — watching, free, awake. Emotional beat: the ghost becomes a guardian.
